title: Sell Mineral Rights in Centerville, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Centerville, PA | Mon Valley
metaDescription: Centerville, PA mineral owners in the Mon Valley: get a plain-English cash offer on your Marcellus royalty, no listing fees, no obligation.
heroLead: Centerville sits in the Mon Valley end of Washington County, small-town country where a lot of mineral ownership still runs through farm families rather than institutions.
intro: Centerville doesn't draw much outside attention, but the surrounding farmland has been part of Washington County's Marcellus leasehold for well over a decade. If your family holds minerals here, it's likely tied to a modest tract that's been passed down a generation or two, with a lease signed sometime during the county's early drilling boom and a royalty check that's arrived, in one form or another, ever since.
We've sat on the other side of a confusing royalty statement ourselves. That's why we start by explaining what your paperwork says rather than jumping straight to a number.

sections.heading: Farm country still producing
paragraphs: This part of the county remains solidly agricultural even with the amount of gas development around it, and many mineral tracts near Centerville are attached to working farms where the family kept the surface and the minerals both. That's a cleaner ownership picture than a lot of split-estate situations elsewhere in the county, but it doesn't make the royalty statement any easier to read.

Wells in this area typically produce wet gas, meaning natural gas liquids are separated out during processing before your royalty is calculated, and that step is where post-production costs show up as a deduction on your statement.

sections.heading: What decline looks like on a real statement
paragraphs: Marcellus wells produce their highest volumes in the first one to three years, then taper off into a longer, slower decline. If your Centerville royalty has dropped noticeably from what it was five or six years ago, that's usually normal well behavior rather than a sign something's wrong, though it's still worth reviewing the actual numbers together.

sections.heading: Selling without upending the family farm
paragraphs: A mineral sale is limited to the subsurface rights and the royalty income they produce; it doesn't touch the surface farmland or require any change to how the property is used or worked.

faqs.question: Will selling my minerals affect farming the surface?
faqs.answer: No. The sale covers only the subsurface mineral rights and royalty income; surface use and farming operations are unaffected.

faqs.question: My royalty has dropped every year since the well started. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically. Marcellus wells decline steeply in the first few years before leveling into a slower tail, and that shows up directly in your check.

faqs.question: Can I sell only a portion of my interest and keep the rest?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can structure an offer for a percentage of your interest if you'd rather keep some exposure to future production.
